Model policy changed by the founder on 2026-09-27: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) at max effort for everything, replacing the earlier strongest-available-model rule. Provenance: the pipeline build, Stage 1 (rooms), Stage 2 (mask, ladder audit) and the Stage 3 round-1 search plans ran on Fable 5.1; the search runners, which only paste queries into the search tool and judge nothing, ran on Sonnet 5 (round 1) or Haiku 4.5. Records are verbatim search titles and URLs, so they do not depend on the model. Every agent started after the switch runs on Opus 5.5 at max effort: agent definitions, skills and workflow scripts pin it.

Switch-over in Stage 3 (founder's message at 08:16 UTC): the five listening workflows already running were left to finish, as the founder asked. Under the new rule 13 the Fable labelers stopped themselves without labeling, including ones started before the switch (they re-read CLAUDE.md), so labels come only from Opus 5.5 unless a labeler already running at 08:16 finished normally (each room's source is logged when the workflows are resumed). On resume, finished search plans and searches replay from the workflow cache (searches return verbatim results, so the runner's model does not matter); labeling, later rounds and synthesis run on Opus 5.5 at max effort. Taxonomy drafts and partial labels left by Fable labelers that did not finish are removed first (they stay in git history), so Opus writes each room's taxonomy itself.

Settings: the repo-root .claude/settings.json now sets model claude-opus-5-5, CLAUDE_CODE_EFFORT_LEVEL=max and CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL=claude-opus-5-5 (plus the web-search cap). This host-managed cloud session ignores CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL, so every agent is also pinned to Opus 5.5 by name.

Listener and walker instructions now keep temporary files in cache/tmp/<unit>/ (git-ignored), because parallel agents shared one scratchpad folder and could overwrite each other's helper files. Label writers check record ids against the room's batch list, so a collision fails loudly instead of mixing rooms.

text: Saturation rule read conservatively (the founder's words: at least 500 records per room, then continue until the last 300 records add no new pain and change no rank). Before this fix the test could pass inside round 1, whose last 300 records are just the plan's last queries (often job posts and official pages with no member voice). Now: (1) saturation is tested only from round 2, so every room collects at least one more round after the first 500+ records; (2) when the latest round brings more than 300 records, the whole round is the window; (3) a window with fewer than 30 member records is not evaluable, because it cannot show a new pain. Rooms that never meet this stop as exhausted (a round adds fewer than 50 new records) or at 8 rounds, and are reported as not saturated. Rules in config/kill_rules.yaml (saturation_from_round, saturation_window_whole_round, saturation_min_member_records); 432 tests pass.

Saturation also counts a pain the taxonomy gains in a round as a new pain in that round. Listeners relabel every batch when the taxonomy changes, so a new pain can land on old records too, and the label counts alone would then miss that the new round revealed it. Detected by added_round and, as a backstop, by comparing with the previous round's list of pain keys. 434 tests pass.

The rule 'at least 3 source kinds per room' was in the config but never checked, and every record's source is 'websearch'. It is now checked by the kind of site each record points to (config/source_kinds.yaml: forum, qa, video, reviews, jobs, official, news, social, blog_or_site; a kind counts with at least 5 records). Round-1 records already span 7-9 kinds in every room. A room below 3 kinds has its pains tagged [source kinds: N] and is listed for review. 437 tests pass.

By then round 1 was fully labeled on Opus in 9 rooms and partly in 3 (active-retail 9/14 batches, salon-spa 9/17, startup-founders 6/11); d2c and outbound had none. The founder said 'Try again' and a test agent ran, so the run continues.

Labeling split into one fresh Opus labeler per batch (about 80 records each), between a label-prep step (scripts, taxonomy, funnel label-todo) and a label-finish step (count, saturation). Reason: the single-agent labelers held a whole room in context (300-440k tokens, 100-155 steps, 15-33 million cached tokens re-read per room), which exhausted the weekly limit; a per-batch labeler needs about 25k tokens. Same model, effort, instructions and records; no sample is reduced. Labelers never edit the taxonomy: they suggest missing pains, a round with suggestions is not counted as saturated, and the next label-prep decides. New commands: count --batch and label-todo (445 tests pass).
